item.text:
## 3B.1 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** **Mixed / partial protection.** Lula’s federal government took some real steps toward restraining state violence and improving accountability, especially on democratic violence and police use-of-force rules. But the 2024 record still shows serious, ongoing police killings and weak compliance with long-standing human-rights rulings. I found no sign of torture/disappearance policy at the federal level, but I also found no evidence that Lula solved the underlying police-violence problem.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula marked the Jan. 8 democracy anniversary by demanding punishment for those who financed, planned, and executed the coup attempt.
  - **Title:** [Brazil marks anniversary of Jan. 8 attack on democracy](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/brazil-to-mark-anniversary-of-january-8-attack-on-democracy-3269163)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
  - **Date:** January 8, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/brazil-to-mark-anniversary-of-january-8-attack-on-democracy-3269163
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said those who financed, planned, and executed the coup attempt must be “exemplarily punished.” This is direct accountability for political violence, and it is the strongest positive item I found for 3B.1.
  - **Question IDs:** `3B.1`; also `2B.3`, `2B.9`, `2B.6`

- **Claim:** The federal government published a report compiling evidence on body cameras as a tool to reduce police lethality.
  - **Title:** [Relatório do MJSP apresenta diagnóstico sobre o uso de câmeras corporais policiais](https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/relatorio-do-mjsp-apresenta-diagnostico-sobre-o-uso-de-cameras-corporais-policiais)
  - **Publisher:** Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública
  - **Date:** July 31, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/relatorio-do-mjsp-apresenta-diagnostico-sobre-o-uso-de-cameras-corporais-policiais
  - **Claim-level summary:** The ministry released a review of studies on body cameras and their relationship to reduced police lethality and more reporting. This is a concrete policy step aimed at reducing arbitrary or excessive force.
  - **Question IDs:** `3B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula signed a decree updating rules on differentiated police force with explicit human-rights language.
  - **Title:** [Decreto que atualiza regras sobre o uso diferenciado da força pelas polícias é publicado](https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/decreto-que-atualiza-regras-sobre-o-uso-diferenciado-da-forca-pelas-policias-e-publicado)
  - **Publisher:** Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública
  - **Date:** December 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/decreto-que-atualiza-regras-sobre-o-uso-diferenciado-da-forca-pelas-policias-e-publicado
  - **Claim-level summary:** The ministry said the decree updated rules for police approaches and less-lethal instruments, with a focus on efficiency, professionalization, and respect for human rights. This is the clearest 2024 federal reform aimed at preventing state violence.
  - **Question IDs:** `3B.1`

- **Claim:** Human Rights Watch said Brazil still had serious police-abuse problems in 2024 and was not fully complying with international rulings.
  - **Title:** [Brazil: Comply with Rulings on Police Violence](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/15/brazil-comply-rulings-police-violence)
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** March 15, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/15/brazil-comply-rulings-police-violence
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW said Brazil should comply with Inter-American Court rulings on police killings, noted that São Paulo raids had already left at least 45 dead after a police officer was killed, and reported credible allegations of unlawful force, intimidation, and evidence tampering. This is strong counterevidence: state violence remained a live problem.
  - **Question IDs:** `3B.1`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s police-violence record was still severe in the background context entering 2024.
  - **Title:** [World Report 2024: Brazil](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/brazil)
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 2024 country report
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/brazil
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW reported 6,429 police killings in 2022 and serious investigation gaps, including deficient forensic work and high police killings in São Paulo. This is background, not Lula-specific proof, but it shows the inherited problem was large and persistent.
  - **Question IDs:** `3B.1`

### Search gap

I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence of:
- torture or disappearances being reduced by federal action,
- meaningful federal accountability for prior extrajudicial killings,
- a specific Lula-led anti-torture initiative,
- or a decisive break with Brazil’s longstanding police-violence problem.

So the best-supported reading is **partial improvement at the federal policy level**, but **insufficient evidence of a transformed human-rights environment**.
